item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 250546
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sat Oct 24 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Vance, located a few hundred miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
Showers and thunderstorms are becoming more organized in association
with a broad area of low pressure located near the International
Date Line, several hundred miles west of Johnston Atoll.
Environmental conditions appear conducive for development over the
next few days, and a tropical depression could form during the early
part of next week while the system moves east-northeastward at 10 to
15 mph. By the middle of next week, however, strong upper-level
winds should limit any additional development.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Vance Public Advisory Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Sun Oct 25 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 250837
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Vance Advisory Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 AM CST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
...VANCE WEAKENS SLIGHTLY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.3N 103.4W
ABOUT 295 MI...475 KM SW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 330 MI...530 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 340 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...980 MB...28.94 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Vance was located 
near latitude 14.3 North, longitude 103.4 West. Vance is moving 
toward the north-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). This slow 
north-northwest to northwest motion is expected to continue the next 
few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast the next couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 980 mb (28.94 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4 
inches of rain, with isolated higher totals of 7 inches possible, 
across Colima and western portions of Michoacán and Jalisco. This 
rainfall may produce flooding and mudslides, especially in areas 
along steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of 
southern and southwestern Mexico the next several days. These swells 
are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Vance Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Sun Oct 25 2026 
ZCZC MIATCDEP2 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
Hurricane Vance Discussion Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 AM CST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
Vance's convective structure continues to be impacted by 
southwesterly wind shear. Showers and thunderstorms have become less 
organized, and most of the convection is now occurring in the 
northern semi-circle. The latest subjective and objective intensity 
estimates range from 62 to 77 kt. Given the ragged satellite 
appearance, the initial intensity is lowered to 75 kt for this 
advisory, and that could be generous.

The system is moving north-northwestward at 340/04 kt, steered 
between a trough over the western United States and the western 
periphery of a mid-level ridge over Mexico. Vance remains in weak 
steering currents, a slow, generally north-northwestward to 
northwestward motion is expected over the next few days. There 
remain some along-track differences in the forward speed of the 
system toward the end of the forecast period, which will be 
dependent on the vertical depth of the vortex at that 
time. The latest NHC track forecast has been shifted westward once 
again, but it remains on the eastern edge of the guidance envelope 
due to continuity constraints, with the HCCA and GDMI aids lying to 
the west of the current track.

Vance will continue to encounter moderate southwesterly wind shear 
and remains in the wake of an abundance of recent cyclones that have 
moved over this area off the southwestern coast of Mexico over the 
past month or so. While oceanic heat content may increase slightly, 
mid-level dry air is forecast to entrain into the circulation, and 
shear should increase even further. This will induce a steadier rate 
of weakening. The NHC intensity forecast trends toward the latest 
HCCA guidance and shows an overall faster rate of weakening than the 
previous advisory. By the end of the forecast period, increasing 
shear and dry air should take their toll on the convection 
organization of Vance. Global models show the system may struggle to 
produce organized deep convection by Day 5, and the latest forecast 
now shows Vance becoming a post-tropical cyclone at that time.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Due to the large uncertainties in both the track and intensity 
forecasts, it is too early to determine what, if any, wind and storm 
surge impacts Vance could bring to the coast of Mexico. Interests in 
southwestern Mexico should continue to monitor the progress of 
Vance.
 
2. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with slow-moving Hurricane 
Vance will impact the western coast of Mexico from Michoacán to 
Jalisco during much of this week. This rainfall may produce flooding 
and mudslides across Colima and western portions of Michoacán and 
Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
